# ARTINEXT

> ARTINEXT is a digital-systems studio based in Iran, working remotely with architecture, structural, and MEP teams. Three service lines: custom Revit/BIM content (parametric families, office libraries, library optimization), custom digital tools (Revit plugins, add-ins, model QA/QC checkers, Dynamo scripts), and workflow automation (process automation, software/data integration, operational dashboards). The site ships in Persian (fa, default) and English (en) at matching URLs — swap the locale segment (`/fa/...` or `/en/...`) for either language.

ARTINEXT does not build off-the-shelf, generic tools. Every project starts from a real, specific workflow problem, not a pre-built product — and the team explicitly turns away work that's just installing a generic plugin without any process review (see `/about`).

## Services

- [Solutions overview](https://artinext.ir/en/solutions): Six services — process automation, custom tool development, dashboards and management systems, BIM/Revit content, modeling and data systems, and AI readiness.
- [Specialist Revit content](https://artinext.ir/en/products/revit-families): Product families, office libraries, project families, and library optimization for real production models, not demo geometry.
- [Custom digital tools](https://artinext.ir/en/products/digital-tools): Custom plugins, model quality control, output management, and data tools shaped around how a specific team actually works.
- [Intelligent automation](https://artinext.ir/en/products/automation): Workflow automation, software/data integration, operational dashboards, and organizational AI assistants, one controlled flow from request to report.
- [Research & Development](https://artinext.ir/en/research-development): Small, fast prototypes used to test an idea before full investment, rather than committing to a build on a guess.

## General (non-geo) service pages

- [Revit Plugin Development](https://artinext.ir/en/revit-plugin-development): Custom Revit plugin development for architecture, structural, and MEP offices across Iran, no city qualifier — for a bare, un-geo-qualified search for the service.
- [Revit Family Creation](https://artinext.ir/en/revit-family-creation): Custom Revit family creation for manufacturers, architecture, and MEP offices across Iran, no city qualifier.
- [AEC Workflow Automation](https://artinext.ir/en/aec-workflow-automation): Workflow automation, software/data integration, and operational dashboards for companies and technical offices across Iran — not Revit-specific, no city qualifier.

## Insights (articles)

- [Choosing a Revit plugin development company](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-plugin-development-company): What actually matters when evaluating a Revit plugin development partner, and where those partnerships usually go wrong.
- [Custom Dynamo script development](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/custom-dynamo-script-development): What a custom Dynamo script actually replaces, and when it's the right tool versus a full Revit API plugin.
- [Where AEC workflow automation should start](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/aec-workflow-automation): How to find the right first process to automate, and why the real ceiling on automation is usually untested rather than fixed.
- [Custom parametric Revit family creation](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/custom-parametric-revit-family-creation): What makes a parametric Revit family actually reliable across real projects, not just functional once in the editor.
- [How much does Revit plugin development cost?](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-plugin-development-cost): What actually drives Revit plugin pricing — workflow complexity, integration needs, and user count — instead of a flat price list.
- [A Revit model checker automates QA/QC — it doesn't replace it](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-model-checker): Why the checkset behind a model checker, not the checker itself, is what makes its report trustworthy.
- [Revit library optimization isn't about deleting files](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-library-optimization): What actually needs fixing in a bloated or inconsistent Revit content library.
